gaps.sentence: The novel had a huge effect on ___ young people of the 1960s.
gaps.explanation: 'The young people of the 1960s' — defined by the of-phrase, so 'the'.

gaps.sentence: They elected her ___ chairperson for a second term.
gaps.explanation: After 'elect/appoint', roles take no article: elected her chairperson.

gaps.sentence: He was born in ___ Netherlands, not in Belgium.
gaps.explanation: Country names that are plural or contain 'Kingdom/Republic/States' take 'the': the Netherlands.

gaps.sentence: My uncle is ___ university lecturer and a painter in his free time.
gaps.explanation: 'A university lecturer' (the u sounds like /juː/); the second gap is also 'an artist'.

gaps.sentence: She spent three weeks in ___ hospital after the accident.
gaps.explanation: British English: be in hospital (as a patient) takes no article; the building is the hospital.

gaps.sentence: ___ Hyde Park is lovely in autumn.
gaps.explanation: Most park names take no article: Hyde Park, Central Park (exception: the Grands Boulevards style names).

gaps.sentence: The thief was sent to ___ prison for three years.
gaps.explanation: 'Sent to prison' — the institution, no article; 'the prison' would mean the building.

gaps.sentence: ___ rich variety of birds lives in the Danube delta.
gaps.explanation: A rich variety of… — variety is countable here, first mention.
